title: Best Chatbot Developers (2026): How to Hire One Safely
description: How to hire a chatbot developer: what the project should include, how to brief it, what drives the price and the red flags to avoid.
intro: A chatbot can answer common questions, book appointments or qualify leads at any hour. It can also give wrong answers with confidence, frustrate customers who want a person, or leak data it should never see. This guide helps you set up a chatbot project with clear limits and a way to hand over to a human.

faq.q: What is the difference between a rule-based and an AI chatbot?
faq.a: A rule-based chatbot follows fixed menus and answers you write in advance. An AI chatbot uses a language model to understand free text and write replies, often based on your own documents. Rule-based bots are predictable; AI bots are more flexible but need careful limits and testing.
On your website, in messaging apps such as WhatsApp, Messenger or Instagram, or inside tools like Slack. Each channel has its own setup and rules, so list every channel you need in the brief.

faq.q: Who pays for the AI and messaging costs?
faq.a: Usually you do, directly to the AI or messaging provider, based on use. Ask the developer to set up these accounts in your name, explain the running costs, and set spending limits.

faq.q: How do I stop the chatbot from making things up?
faq.a: Give it a limited set of approved information, tell it to say when it does not know, and test it with difficult questions before launch. A clear way to reach a human is essential.

faq.q: What about customer data and privacy?
faq.a: Decide what the chatbot may collect and where conversations are stored. Tell users they are talking to a bot, and check the privacy rules that apply to your business and your customers' countries.
